title: Truth Needs More Than One Voice

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: One witness is not enough to convict anyone accused of any crime or offense they may have committed. A matter must be established by the testimony of two or three witnesses. - Deut 19:15 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God builds a vital safeguard into His justice, no one could be convicted on the word of a single witness. A serious charge required two or three witnesses to establish the truth. This protected people from being condemned by one person's lie, mistake, or grudge. God knew how easily a single false accusation could destroy an innocent life.

This law reveals God's deep concern for truth and fairness. He does not want His people acting on unverified claims or rushing to judgment based on one voice. Truth is precious, and God surrounds it with protections so that the innocent are not wrongly condemned.

This principle carries into the New Testament and into wise living today. Jesus applied it to resolving conflicts in the community, taking one or two others along so that every matter could be established (Matt 18:16). We honour God when we refuse to spread or believe accusations based on a single unverified source. In a world full of quick opinions and rushed judgments, God's people are called to be careful, fair, and slow to condemn. How often do we believe the worst about someone based on one person's word? God calls us to a higher standard of truth. Are you careful to seek the full truth before forming judgments about others?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you rush to judgment on one person's word?
2. How can you be more careful with accusations you hear?
3. Where do you need to seek the full truth before deciding?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, help me love truth and refuse to condemn others on a single voice. Make me fair, patient, and careful in judgment. Amen.
